findings.source_quote: πόσοις κατ’ ὄναρ ὁμοίως ἄλλοις ὤφθησαν καὶ ὕπαρ συναντήσαντες ἀλλήλοις πρὸς τὸ κατ’ ὄναρ ἀντιβάλλοντες οὐ συνεφώνησαν;
findings.english_quote: To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams, and, when those people met one another while awake and compared what they had seen in dreams, did not agree?
findings.issue: The English does not clearly establish the subject of 'did not agree' after shifting from the appearing beings to their human recipients. It also reads as asking how many recipients disagreed. The Greek negative question can instead invite assent that the recipients agreed: 'did they not agree?' This material distinction in rhetorical force, together with the subject shift from ὤφθησαν to the recipients understood in the subsequent participles and verb, is not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: A clearer candidate is: 'To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams—and, when those people met one another while awake and compared their dream experiences, did those people not agree?' Add a note explaining the understood change of subject and the rhetorical interpretation of οὐ συνεφώνησαν. Preserve the disagreement interpretation as a material alternative rather than treating either interpretation as uniquely established. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν
findings.english_quote: Thus that is no longer an apparition in a dream
findings.issue: The nominal interpretation of ἐπιφανείη is defensible, but the note discusses only the noun-versus-optative distinction. A materially different nominal construction remains undisclosed: οὐκέτι ὄναρ can deny that the experience is a dream, followed by the positive predication that it is a manifestation. The draft instead denies its being an apparition in a dream. These readings differ in what is denied and affirmed, and the distinction matters particularly when interpreting the preceding agreement question.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to distinguish the chosen adverbial reading of ὄναρ from the alternative, 'Thus it is no longer a dream; that is a manifestation,' which understands an elliptical copula in the first predication. Explain the contextual reason for the main choice and review this clause together with the preceding question. Preserve the supplied spelling and punctuation as edition features; neither this ambiguity nor the proposed interpretive punctuation requires an invented restoration.
